translate_en|mods/ViewpointALife/42/medi: Answer an NPC / talk at the door

Presses A-Life's "Answer ..." or "Talk to ... at the door" button in first and third person, so you don't have to unlock the mouse. If it's the same key as the NPC menu's, the menu gets it while the crosshair is on an NPC. On a controller, A presses it.
Click one corner of the area
Click the opposite corner (right-click to start over)
Answer / Talk button above the hotbar, with key hint
Ticked: the button sits above the hotbar and shows the answer key, like "[G] Answer Bob". Unticked: A-Life's own button, placement and label. The answer key works either way.
Debug log (DO NOT USE THIS, MAY CAUSE LAG)

(DO NOT USE THIS, MAY CAUSE LAG) Writes what the crosshair NPC menu is doing to console.txt every few seconds (lines start with [ViewpointALifeCompat] status). Turn it on only when asked for a bug report.
Equip
Open / close the A-Life Jeem faction window
People, bases and the rest of the Jeem extension's window. Works in every view.
Show Jeem's menu options on a controller

Adds Trade, Equip and Medical Check to the crosshair NPC menu while you play with a controller. Their windows come from the Jeem extension and don't support controllers, so you need the mouse to use and close them.

NPC menu: select key
Picks the highlighted row of the crosshair NPC menu in first and third person. F by default; while the menu is up this key doesn't toggle your flashlight.
None
Mouse & keyboard: NPC menu aim area
How far from an NPC the crosshair can be for their menu to open while you play with mouse and keyboard. 1 is right on their body; higher is easier to hit.
NPC menu: next row key

Moves the highlight to the next row of the crosshair NPC menu, like the mouse wheel. Unbound by default; set it if another mod uses your wheel or you have none. Pick a key that is free in your setup and not the select key.
Outline the NPC you aim at
Draws the yellow outline on the NPC under the crosshair. Off: the NPC menu still appears, without the outline.
Keep NPC speech overhead when A-Life's speech boxes are on

Only matters when A-Life's own "Boxed NPC speech" option is on (it is off by default, and then speech is always overhead text). Ticked: NPC lines still float above the speaker's head in 3D. Unticked: A-Life's speech box near the bottom of the screen.
